question: If, x + y = 7 and xy = 10 then the value of x² + y² is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the identity: x² + y² = (x + y)² − 2xy

Given: x + y = 7 and xy = 10

⇒ x² + y² = 7² − 2 × 10

⇒ x² + y² = 49 − 20 = 29

**∴ Answer = 29**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

x + y = 7 and xy = 10

**Formula used:**

x² + y² = (x + y)² − 2xy

**Calculations:**

⇒ Substitute: x² + y² = (7)² − 2 × 10

⇒ Simplify: x² + y² = 49 − 20 = 29

**∴ The correct answer is 29.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Related Identity: Expansion Formula

(x + y)² = x² + y² + 2xy

Sum and Product of Roots

For quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0, sum of roots = −b/a and product of roots = c/a.

Difference of Squares

x² − y² = (x + y)(x − y)

Useful Identity

x² + y² = (x + y)² − 2xy
